claim: Fixed the RNG-determinism bug in classify_omission_units_jitter.py / classify_omission_units_condition.py (root cause of the raw-value discrepancy flagged unresolved in artifacts/.lab/bh-fdr-backwards-divisor-fix-20260814.json). While isolating the BH-fix-only delta on the now-deterministic data, found a second, more serious, previously-hidden problem specific to classify_omission_units_jitter.py.

rng_fix.root_cause: Both scripts shared one np.random.default_rng(42) across their whole sorted-session loop, consumed sequentially per unit inside analyse_session -- a session's result depended on which OTHER sessions ran before it. Adding the 22nd session shifted every later session's draws.
rng_fix.fix: Per-session RNG seeded from (BASE_SEED, zlib.crc32(filename)) -- deterministic and independent of corpus membership/order/size by construction. zlib.crc32 used deliberately instead of Python's hash() (which is randomized per-interpreter-run via PYTHONHASHSEED and would not even be reproducible run-to-run).
rng_fix.verified: Both scripts rerun end-to-end on the full 22-session corpus without error.

bh_isolation_condition_script.method: Recomputed q-values from the current (deterministic) run's own raw p_rate values under the OLD buggy divisor (np.arange(n,0,-1)) and diffed against the corrected classification -- isolates the BH-fix-only effect with corpus and RNG both held fixed.
bh_isolation_condition_script.result: ALPHA=0.025. Correct BH: O+ 133, O- 454. Buggy BH on the SAME data: O+ 348, O- 820. The bug was purely liberal (under-corrected -> inflated significance) by +215 O+ and +366 O- false calls -- consistent with a backwards/smaller denominator producing smaller q-values.
bh_isolation_condition_script.status: resolved -- current O+ 133 / O- 454 (ALPHA=0.025) is the correct, trustworthy number for this script.

NEW_FINDING_jitter_script_structurally_c.severity: high -- affects every historical O+/O-/O++ number ever produced by this specific script
NEW_FINDING_jitter_script_structurally_c.observation: Full 22-session rerun (RNG fix + already-correct BH) classifies ALL 9,056 units as 'ns'. Zero O+, zero O-, zero O++, in every area.
NEW_FINDING_jitter_script_structurally_c.mechanism: p_rate/p_ramp are permutation p-values with a hard floor: p = (1 + count_as_extreme) / (N_SHUFFLES + 1) = 1/1001 = 0.000999 at best, N_SHUFFLES=1000. Only 13 of 9056 units ever reach that floor (min p_rate observed: 0.0009990009990009, exactly 1/1001). At n=9056 and ALPHA=0.01, BH's rank-1 significance threshold is ~1.1e-6 -- roughly 900x smaller than the floor this test can ever produce. With only 13 units at the floor (not enough to form a large tied block the BH step-up procedure can walk down to), none survive correction. This is NOT a bug in the corrected bh() code, nor a regression from the RNG fix -- it is a genuine, previously-hidden mathematical consequence of pairing a 1000-shuffle permutation test with a 9056-unit single BH family at alpha=0.01. The OLD buggy (backwards-divisor) bh() was silently masking this by being far more liberal, which is presumably why this was never noticed before Phase 0's fix.
NEW_FINDING_jitter_script_structurally_c.contrast_with_condition_script: classify_omission_units_condition.py uses the identical floor formula and N_SHUFFLES=1000, but 587/9056 units hit the floor (a much larger, more prevalent effect -- omission-vs-real-stimulus contrast, not a narrow temporal-jitter-null contrast). BH's tie-handling lets that large tied block survive collectively, which is why the condition script still returns real (O+ 133, O- 454), non-zero classifications while the jitter script returns none.
NEW_FINDING_jitter_script_structurally_c.implication: Every prior omission_jitter_units.csv / omission_jitter_by_area.csv / omission_jitter_by_area_animal.csv number (O+/O-/O++ counts or percentages) attributed to this specific script should be treated as unusable going forward under the correct BH code, until the test's resolution or correction scope is revisited -- not just the numbers changed by this session's reruns, ALL of them, historically, back to whenever the BH bug was introduced.
NEW_FINDING_jitter_script_structurally_c.NOT_decided_here: How to fix this is a real methodological choice with real cost tradeoffs, not decided unilaterally in this session: (a) increase N_SHUFFLES substantially (rough estimate: need N_SHUFFLES on the order of >>n/alpha to give the floor enough resolution -- current run already took ~28 minutes for 22 sessions with N_SHUFFLES=1000 and onset detection disabled; scaling shuffles up materially multiplies runtime), (b) narrow the BH correction family (e.g. per-area rather than pooling all 10 areas x 9056 units into one family -- changes what 'FDR-controlled' means and needs to be a deliberate, documented choice), (c) relax ALPHA, (d) accept that this specific jitter-null design is underpowered at unit-level granularity on this corpus and is not the right tool for this question. Flagged for Hamm's decision.

outputs_this_session: outputs/classification/omission_jitter_units.csv (rerun, RNG-fixed, correct BH: all-null -- see finding above, --no-onset was used for speed; onset-latency sub-analysis not rerun)
